items.heading: There Is No Universal Winner
items.text: There is no universal winner here, and most comparison articles pick a side too fast because "writer" sounds like one job when it is really two very different careers wearing the same word.

items.heading: Most People Compare Journalism
items.text: Most people compare journalism and content writing using the word "writer" as if the daily reality were the same. It is not.

items.heading: The Two Fields Also Differ
items.text: The two fields also differ sharply in how you actually get your first paid assignment.

visuals.heading: What the Daily Work Actually Looks Like

rows: Chase a story, verify facts with at least two sources, interview people, file a report against a hard deadline that someone else sets.
Research a topic, write to a brief a marketing team gave you, target a keyword, and hand in a draft against a deadline you usually had a say in.
A source cancels an hour before deadline, a fact will not confirm, or a story competes with five other outlets covering the same event.
A client changes the brief midway, an AI-generated first draft needs a full rewrite, or a piece needs to rank on Google and read well for humans at the same time.
An editor, a news desk, and ultimately the public record, accuracy and attribution carry legal and reputational weight.
A client, a marketing manager, or an editorial calendar, the piece needs to serve a business goal, not just inform.
News reports, investigations, features, explainers, or on-camera segments published under your byline.
Blog posts, website copy, product descriptions, email sequences, social captions, or long-form guides, usually unbylined or lightly credited.

figures.label: Pay Range
figures.source: A visible byline at a well-known outlet does not always come with strong pay, especially at regional channels where salaries can sit at Rs 15,000-30,000 a month. Check actual entry-level pay at the specific outlets you are targeting, not the outlet's brand reputation.
